jobs.title: Director, Financial Operations
Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
Job Purpose

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation leads the development and execution of the organization’s enterprise AI strategy and transformation agenda to drive measurable business value, productivity, operational efficiency, innovation, and informed decision-making. The role serves as the organization’s AI subject matter expert and enterprise coordinating point, providing strategic guidance on AI opportunities, investments, governance, risk, technology, adoption, and value realization.

The Director partners with business and functional leaders to identify, prioritize, and implement AI and intelligent automation opportunities aligned with organizational objectives and financial goals. The role initially focuses on leveraging AI to enhance financial and operational performance, including forecasting, reporting, analysis, productivity, workflow efficiency, cost management, and decision-making, with successful capabilities and practices progressively expanded across other functions. The Director oversees the enterprise AI portfolio and lifecycle from opportunity assessment and business case development through solution selection, implementation, adoption, benefits realization, ongoing monitoring, and retirement.

Key Duties And Responsibilities

AI Strategy, Portfolio & Value Management

Develop and maintain the enterprise AI strategy, operating model, portfolio, and roadmap aligned with corporate objectives and financial goals.
Identify, evaluate, and prioritize AI opportunities based on strategic alignment, business value, cost, complexity, data readiness, risk, and organizational readiness.
Develop business cases, investment recommendations, and implementation roadmaps, including build, buy, configure, or partner options.
Establish performance measures, baseline metrics, and value-realization frameworks to track AI adoption, ROI, productivity, cost savings, revenue impact, and other business outcomes.
Provide executive leadership with visibility into AI investments, performance, realized benefits, opportunities, and risks.

AI Solution Development & Implementation

Lead the evaluation, design, development, and deployment of AI solutions across enterprise productivity, function-specific applications, intelligent automation, advanced AI, and emerging agentic capabilities.
Partner with business units and end users to identify opportunities, develop practical AI-enabled solutions, and improve processes and ways of working.
Oversee AI pilots, proofs of concept, and enterprise implementations through the full lifecycle—from opportunity identification and feasibility through deployment, adoption, benefits realization, monitoring, and retirement.
Coordinate with Cybersecurity, Human Resources and other stakeholders to ensure solutions are appropriately designed, implemented, adopted, and measured.
Assess solution performance and recommend whether initiatives should be scaled, enhanced, consolidated, paused, or retired based on business value, adoption, cost, and risk.

AI Governance, Risk & Responsible Adoption

Establish and maintain enterprise AI governance frameworks, policies, standards, controls, and risk-based processes to support responsible AI adoption.
Ensure AI initiatives are appropriately assessed for cybersecurity, privacy, data, intellectual property, legal, ethical, third-party, model, and business continuity risks.
Maintain an enterprise inventory of approved AI technologies, platforms, models, agents, and material use cases, with appropriate review, approval, testing, human oversight, monitoring, and escalation requirements.
Ensure data quality, classification, access, security, information governance, and regulatory requirements are addressed before AI solutions are deployed.
Monitor the evolving AI landscape, regulatory expectations, and associated risks, and update governance practices as required.

Enterprise AI Adoption & Change Management

Lead enterprise AI literacy, adoption, and change-management initiatives across executives, leaders, employees, technical teams, and advanced AI users.
Develop and deliver role- and function-specific training, guidance, and resources to promote effective and responsible use of AI.
Serve as the enterprise resource for AI strategy, best practices, use-case guidance, and adoption support.
Measure AI utilization, adoption, training effectiveness, employee feedback, and business outcomes to continuously improve AI enablement.
Coordinate internal subject matter experts, technology teams, business stakeholders, and external partners to support successful AI adoption

Vendor, Technology & Partner Management

Evaluate AI technologies, vendors, consultants, platforms, and implementation partners against business requirements, value, security, architecture, scalability, risk, and total cost of ownership.
Manage AI technology and vendor relationships to ensure service quality, effective implementation, and value realization.
Maintain oversight of the enterprise AI technology portfolio to identify duplicate capabilities, unnecessary licensing, overlapping solutions, and opportunities for consolidation.
Monitor emerging AI technologies—including generative AI, large language models, predictive AI, intelligent automation, computer vision, and agentic AI—and assess their practical business applicability and potential value.

Qualifications, Skills, And Educational Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred.
Minimum seven (7) years of progressive experience in AI, data analytics, digital transformation, automation, technology, or related fields, including significant experience leading enterprise AI or generative AI adoption.
Proven experience leading complex, enterprise-wide AI or business transformation initiatives from strategy and business case development through implementation, adoption, scaling, and measurable value realization.
Strong business and financial acumen, including experience with budgeting, forecasting, reporting, business case development, technology investment evaluation, performance measurement, and ROI.
Strong knowledge of AI technologies, including generative AI, machine learning, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, large language models, AI agents, and emerging AI capabilities, with an understanding of data, cybersecurity, privacy, and AI governance.
Strong strategic thinking, analytical, communication, stakeholder management, project management, and change management skills, with the ability to translate complex technology into practical business solutions and influence cross-functional decisions.
Strong technical and business judgment to evaluate AI solutions, vendors, risks, data and technology dependencies, and investment decisions. Professional certifications in AI, analytics, project management, responsible AI, or AI governance are considered an asset.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS

Standard office setting - hybrid arrangement (4 days in-office)
Fast paced office environment
Travel expectations between facilities in Mississauga and North York

jobs.title: Head of Finance
jobs.description:
$150,000–$180,000 a year

Tuition reimbursement, Paid time off, Vision care, Dental care, Life insurance, Employee assistance program, Disability insurance, Discounted or free food

Permanent, Full-time

Hybrid work in 4445 Lougheed Highway W, Burnaby, BC

About Us:

Entertainment Partners is a global organization that has been a trusted production partner to the entertainment industry for over 45 years, helping clients create and produce great shows, choose the best production location, forecast, manage and track expenses, and pay crew and talent. As a global leader in entertainment payroll, production finance and production management solutions, EP delivers integrated, digital solutions to support every phase of production. EP brings together background casting and digital production technology with the Casting Portal, the leading SaaS-based platform that has transformed the way background actors are found, hired, managed and paid, and the iconic and legendary Central Casting.
Entertainment Partners Canada is the lead provider of financial services to the entertainment industry in Canada. We provide financial services to the Motion Picture, Television and Commercial industries along with production management and accounting software services. Entertainment Partners Canada prides itself on being the best in class from a product/services perspective but we are equally proud to have been Great Places to Work certified since 2017, providing an encouraging, accepting, and interesting work experience for all of our valued employees.
Job Summary:

The candidate is EP Canada's senior finance leader — strategic partner to the Canadian leadership team and primary Canadian counterpart to EP's global finance and FP&A organizations. The role delivers Canadian financial planning, analysis, and reporting capability into a global FP&A framework, and is accountable for controllership, statutory reporting, cash management, and the integrity of all Canadian accounting systems, controls, and financial information.
Working closely with the President, Canada and department leaders across Sales, Client Services, Payroll, Incentives, Operations, HR, and Technology, the candidate turns operating information into forecasts, business cases, and business narrative that shape investment, pricing, and resourcing decisions. In parallel, the role partners daily with the global FP&A team on planning, forecasting, and management reporting, and with the broader finance organization — CFO, Corporate Controller, Tax, and Treasury — to ensure Canadian results are reported accurately, forecasts are aligned to global planning cadences, and cross-border obligations are met.
The candidate adheres to the accounting policies and procedures approved by the CFO, company leadership, and Board of Directors and ensures the integrity of all accounting systems and financial information. The Candidate's duties are performed consistently with the company's mission and values, and must adhere to company policies and procedures.
Key Duties and Responsibilities:

Strategic partnership with Canadian leadership:

Serve as strategic finance partner/advisor to the President, Canada and the Canadian leadership team, providing financial analysis, recommendations, and decision support on investment, pricing, resourcing, and other business-critical decisions.
Partner with Canadian department leaders across Sales, Client Services, Payroll, Incentives, Operations, HR, and Technology; translate operating information into financial insight and support business cases, ROI analyses, and pricing and margin reviews for new and existing service lines.
Serve on the EP Canada Senior Management team and other policy-making committees, representing the financial and commercial implications of business decisions.

Canadian controllership and Partnership with Global Finance:

Acts as the senior Canadian finance leader, ensuring local results are accurately represented within EP's global reporting following all statutory rules and standards.
Serves as the key liaison with US Tax, external auditors, and regulatory bodies (CRA, provincial ministries) on cross-border and compliance matters. (examples: T106, T1134, Part XIII withholding, and ULC-specific treatment)
Responsible for annual audit
Owns the full close-to-reporting cycle for Canada, from general ledger through statutory financial statements, under both Canadian and US GAAP frameworks.
Maintains the control environment — internal controls, segregation of duties, and account reconciliations — underpinning the integrity of Canadian financial reporting.
Partners with Finance Operations to ensure payment and transactional processes are timely, accurate, and well-controlled.
Brings a continuous improvement lens to the close process, starting with a 90-day current state assessment and roadmap.

Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) — Canadian delivery:

Serve as the Canadian finance lead, partnering with global FP&A team and working within the planning framework, calendar, and templates; personally deliver the Canadian components of the annual operating plan, quarterly reforecast, monthly variance analysis, multi-year planning, and scenario modelling.
Own Canadian financial data quality and the Canadian forecasting rhythm across revenue, margin, headcount, capital expenditure, and cash; identify risks and opportunities against plan and surface them to Canadian leadership and global FP&A.
Partner with the global FP&A team on management reporting, KPIs, and dashboards; ensure the Canadian view is accurate, current, and appropriately contextualized in consolidated reporting.
Prepare and present financial updates for board packages, quarterly business reviews, annual operating plans, quarterly forecasts, and town halls.

Treasury, cash, and risk management:

Oversee the local cash management function including maintaining Canadian banking relationships; monitor corporate cash flows, fraud detection, vendor credit risk profiles, and forecast restricted/unrestricted cash balances, and recommend foreign exchange and hedging actions in coordination with Global Treasury.
Manage insurance coverage for the organization in coordination with US Risk Management, including compliance obligations.

Team leadership and continuous improvement:

Lead, develop, and evaluate the Canadian finance team, including recruitment, training, and succession planning; make recommendations on salary increases and annual bonus amounts.
Lead change and continuous improvement initiatives across finance systems, processes, and reporting to support the business's evolving needs, including ERP and reporting system enhancements.
Set and implement short-term and long-term departmental goals, objectives, policies, and operating procedures.
Perform other related duties as needed.

Qualifications:

Essential:

Ten years+ progressive experience in a senior-level finance or accounting position
CPA designation required
Experience operating in the Canadian entity of a US-parented multinational, including US GAAP consolidation and cross-border reporting into a US head office.
Demonstrated experience partnering with executive or senior leadership on business-critical decisions, translating financial analysis into commercial and operational recommendations.
Strong hands-on operational finance capability — management reporting and analysis, scenario modelling — with the ability to personally deliver the work, not only supervise others doing it; experience operating as the local FP&A partner within a global/head-office-led FP&A framework is strongly preferred.
Strong financial storytelling and executive presentation skills — able to translate results and forecasts into clear business narrative that lands with both a Canadian President and the global executive team.
Track record of out-of-the-box thinking when challenged with process improvement, re-organization, major system rehaul
Working knowledge of Canadian tax (T2, GST/HST/PST), statutory reporting, and audit; familiarity with transfer pricing and cross-border tax obligations.
Strong ERP and reporting systems experience.
Executive-level communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders outside of Finance (written and verbal).
Ability to lead teams to produce quality output within tight timeframes and manage multiple concurrent priorities.
Commercial or operational business acumen beyond core accounting and finance, with comfort operating in a matrix organization.

Preferred:

Familiarity with the film and television production ecosystem or experience adjacent to production companies, studios, or service providers.
Experience with Oracle ERP
Private equity-owned or PE-backed environment experience.
Comfort operating across the three-hour Toronto/Vancouver time difference and asynchronously with a US head office.

Why Work with EP:

Group RRSP
Extended health and dental benefits
Hybrid work environment
Casual dress code
Employee snack program
Health and Wellness Spending Account
Movie ticket reimbursement
Employee Assistance Program
Calm app subscription
Work lunches and events
Paid time off (Vacation, sick, volunteer and personal days and additional holiday time)
Tuition reimbursement
Commitment to employee growth and development
Discretionary bonus
Employee Value Plan
Family planning support
Employee Incentive Plan (grants for stellar performance)

Working conditions

Conditions are normal for an office environment
Hybrid work

Compensation

This position offers an expected compensation of $150,000–$180,000 per year, depending on skills and experience. This range reflects the anticipated salary for the successful candidate and complies with Ontario’s pay transparency requirements.
Use of artificial intelligence in our hiring process

Entertainment Partners Canada uses an AI-enabled tool to help screen and assess applications for this position. The tool reviews resumes against the qualifications and requirements in this posting and ranks applications based on job-related criteria. Hiring decisions are made by our recruitment team, who review all applications shortlisted applications and make the final decision.
Commitment to Supporting Accessibility Needs

EP Canada welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. As only short-listed candidates will be contacted, we thank you in advance for your interest in EP!
Please note that only qualified candidates will be considered, and we'll only be following up directly with those selected for next steps.
Pay: $150,000.00-$180,000.00 per year
Benefits:
Casual dress
Company events
Dental care
Disability insurance
Discounted or free food
Employee assistance program
Extended health care
Life insurance
Paid time off
RRSP match
Tuition reimbursement
Vision care
Wellness program
Work from home

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Burnaby, BC
